description: Book one of the open times for the customer. The business then either confirms it at once or receives it as a request it approves (or, for a business that takes its bookings by email, confirms with the customer itself); the answer says which, what happens next, and a `manage.token` to check or cancel the booking later. The customer is emailed. Confirm the service, the time and the customer's details with the customer before calling it. `idempotency_key` is required: choose a new random one for each booking (a UUID without hyphens) and send the same one to retry after a timeout, so a retry cannot make a second booking.

inputSchema.description: Book. The same checks as the business's booking page: a real open start, the questions the card lists, the same limits on every text.

answers.notes: We lose leads that message after hours.
pains: Hours of admin and data entry

agent.description: Who is booking, so the business sees that an agent made the booking and which one.

acting_for.description: Optional: the person it acts for, if that is not the customer.

answers.description: Answers to the questions the card lists under booking.answers, by their `id`. Each question there says its exact format and shows an example that passes: a select takes exactly one of its option strings, copied character for character; a multiselect takes a list of its option strings (at most its `maxSelections`, each once); a text, a long text, an email, a phone number and a web address each have a stated length limit; a select with `allowOther` takes "Other" with the customer's own words under `<id>_other`; and a question with a `none` phrase takes exactly that phrase when there is no answer. A business that comes to the customer (a mobile detailer or tint shop) asks for `address`: check it first (POST /agent/address, the MCP tool check_address) and send the `address` that answers. The address is checked again here, and refused with `address_invalid`, `address_unconfirmed` (with the corrected address) or `outside_service_area`. When Google could not confirm it or corrected it, and the customer says theirs is right as they gave it, send theirs with `address_confirmed: true`: it is filed as given, for the business to check (never past `outside_service_area`). Leave out when the card lists none.

customer.description: The person the booking is for. They receive the confirmation email.

phone.description: Optional, unless the business's questions say it is required.

time_zone.description: Optional IANA zone of the customer ("Europe/London"): a meeting's confirmation then shows their clock too.

idempotency_key.description: Required. A key you choose, new for each booking: 32 to 255 letters, digits, dashes or underscores, and RANDOM, never a counter, a word or a pattern (a UUID without hyphens is right; a key with fewer than 8 distinct characters is refused). Calling book again with the same key and customer email answers the first booking again, with the same manage token, instead of making a second one: use it to retry safely after a timeout.

items.description: What is being booked. May be left out only when the business offers exactly one service (a consulting business's one kind of call). A window tint business takes `tint` instead, never items.

One service being booked. Use the `slug` of a service from the business card. For a business that works on a car, give each car its package and any add-ons as separate items that share the same `label` (the car, as a person would say it: "2023 Porsche 911"), and a `label` is required on every item.

label.description: What the service is for: the car ("2023 Porsche 911"). Required for a detailing business; leave out for a meeting.

slug.description: The service's slug, from the card's services list.

start.description: A start time from `times`, ISO 8601 with an offset, on a whole minute: seconds, when written, are 00 ("2026-10-12T10:00:00-07:00" or "2026-10-12T17:00Z"). It is checked again, and refused with `time_not_open` if it is no longer open.

tint.description: What is being booked at a window tint business, in place of `items` (the card says which a business takes): the class of the customer's car, the windows, the film and the shade, each chosen from the card's `tint` section. The business prices and times it; a shade never changes the price. Choosing the front two windows and the rear sides books the full vehicle, at its price.

film.description: The film: a slug from the card's tint.films.

glass.description: The windows to tint: slugs from the card's tint.glass, each once.

shade.description: The percentage of light the film lets through (lower is darker), for every window: one of the chosen film's shades.

vehicle_class.description: The class of the customer's car: an id from the card's tint.vehicleClasses, each of which lists example models.

zone_shades.description: Optional: a different shade for a window group the chosen glass covers, by the group's id from the card's tint.windowGroups ({"fr": 35, "rr": 20}). Each is one of the film's shades; a group left out takes `shade`.
